q: What is the carbon footprint of honey per kg?
title: Honey carbon footprint per kg
short: Count the transport of hives and honey, heating and filtering energy, and the jar or bottle. Divide by kilograms packed. Bee-keeping itself uses little energy, so for honey the glass jar and road transport are often most of the footprint; sugar feeding in lean seasons adds a little.

ul: Migratory beekeeping moves hives by truck between crops: count the diesel or hire trips.
Sugar fed to colonies in lean months.
Hive boxes and frames, spread over their years of use.
Heating, filtering and moisture reduction: electricity or LPG.

p: A glass jar can weigh about as much as the honey in a small pack. PET or pouches are lighter. State the pack in your figure.

example.title: Worked example: honey plant per kg (one month)
lines: Collection truck diesel: 500 litres x 2.68 = 1,340 kg CO2
Plant total: 4,180 / 20,000 = 0.209 kg CO2 per kg
Add jars, caps and labels for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
